🎰 EU Orders Apps To Be Less Addictive; Users Refresh The Announcement 400 Times

BRUSSELS — reported between two infinite scrolls

REGULATION — Europe is moving to rein in what it calls "addictive design" at Meta — a bold plan to make apps less compelling that regulators announced, then checked their phones, then announced again.

"We want technology that respects your time," an official said, thumb hovering over a pull-to-refresh. Meta responded that its designs are merely "aggressively engaging," and that the little red notification dot is, if anything, a form of fine art.

Experts warn that a truly non-addictive app is technically just a calendar, and no human has downloaded one of those on purpose since 2004.
